neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Jonathan Haidt
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: Religion's possible evolutionary role does not directly prove present moral value, but it reveals psychological and social goods that a flourishing assessment must include.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: An adaptation for group solidarity may have enabled large non-kin societies and may still support happiness, satisfaction, and less selfish social structures even if law can replace parts of it.

inferenceSummary.premise: Adaptations can disclose durable psychological needs and social mechanisms without being normatively authoritative.
inferenceSummary.inference: Those mechanisms are evidence about which forms of life flourish and cannot be dismissed merely because doctrines are false.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: A well-being analysis needs a full descriptive picture of religion's benefits before recommending its removal.

sourceSpan.excerpt: if religion is an adaptation as i believe it is then it could still be true that it was necessary for getting us to where we are and i do believe that religion and the psychology of religion helps explain how we and only we made the transition um to living in large-scale societies of non-kin it could still be the case that it was useful back in tribal days and now we've supplanted it with law and other things so i i would never say that religion being an adaptation or the truth of multi-level selection would prove anything about how we ought to live today but what i do draw from it is that seeing it as an adaptation for group solidarity and group coherence makes it easier to see some of the psychological benefits and socio-structural benefits that might be there that are hard to see if you're a secular person on the left because that is what i see is it's really hard to understand what's good about the other side once you're in a an argument or debate with them and from reading scholarship on religion from reading books especially the book um james alt has this wonderful book spirit and flesh that really helps you see the sociology of a small evangelical community so that's my only point i wouldn't say i draw normative implications directly but i do draw implications for what kinds of lives are happy and satisfying what kinds of social patterns and structures make people less selfish and more inclined to think about others and there i think it you just have to think twice if you're going to say religion's just bad and it makes people do bad things get rid of it yeah well so

neighboringSourceContext.speaker: Jonathan Haidt
neighboringSourceContext.claimSummary: A workable global order should preserve strong lower-level groups within nested institutions rather than erase group boundaries, because evolved tribal psychology constrains feasible arrangements.
neighboringSourceContext.reasonSummary: Haidt contrasts a single borderless community with authority at lower levels, strong families and communities, and a legal architecture coordinating families, states, and countries; evolution does not determine right but informs what is likely to work.

inferenceSummary.premise: Humans are deeply groupish, and social orders can coordinate strong lower-level groups through nested legal and institutional structures.
inferenceSummary.inference: Guidance that ignores this psychology is less feasible, while nested arrangements use rather than deny durable group dispositions.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: Rational moral guidance should treat nested institutions as more workable than abolishing group boundaries.
